questions.q: In a short shipment, what quantity does Oracle Fusion typically invoice?
options: The originally ordered quantity, regardless of what shipped
An average of ordered and shipped quantities
The actual quantity that was confirmed as shipped
Zero, until the full quantity ships
questions.explain: Oracle Fusion invoices the confirmed shipped quantity, not the originally ordered quantity.

questions.q: Why does a 15% discount request need a true approval rather than just proceeding automatically?
options: Because it exceeds standard pricing policy and is not covered by an automatic discount rule
Because all discounts require approval, even the standard 5% rule
Because the customer is new
Because 15% is always illegal
questions.explain: A discount beyond standard, pre-approved rules requires a manual override routed through an approval process.

questions.q: What is the first correct step when a customer disputes an invoice, claiming they were billed for goods they never received?
options: Immediately write off the full balance without investigation
Ignore the dispute until the invoice becomes past due
Cancel the customer's account
Compare the invoice back to the shipment it originated from
questions.explain: Investigating the invoice against its source shipment (the reconciliation checkpoint) comes before deciding whether a credit is warranted.

questions.q: What is the correct way to handle a customer's duplicate payment on the same invoice?
options: Delete the second receipt entirely since it wasn't needed
Retain it as an on-account credit for future use, or refund it — never simply delete it
Apply it to a completely unrelated customer's account
Ignore it; it will resolve itself
questions.explain: Real cash arrived and must be accounted for — as an on-account credit or a refund, not deleted.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a credit check hold and a price override approval, as illustrated by these scenarios?
options: There is no difference between them
A hold always requires a manager's signature
A hold is applied automatically by the system; an approval requires a person to actively say yes before proceeding
An approval is applied automatically without anyone reviewing it
questions.explain: Holds are automatic system stops; approvals require an actual person to review and authorize before the action proceeds.
